newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt mixed, Brazil down on scandal report.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt mixed, Brazil down on scandal report.

text.p: Brady debt remained mixed in heavy trading Tuesday afternoon, with much attention focused on bribery allegations in Brazil, market experts said.
"Volume is very heavy and spreads are mainly tighter," one trader said. While Brazil debt widened 10 to 15 basis points, Mexico, Argentina and Brazil spreads all narrowed, he said.

Brazil C were off a full point at 76 bid after a Brasilia newspaper alleged that five congressmen had accepted payoffs to vote in favor of a proposed amendment allowing government officials to run for reelection.
A Senate committee considering the bill suspended its activities for 24 hours after the report in Folha de Sao Paolo.
New York analysts said the news should have little long-term impact on Brazil debt because it does not appear to implicate the Federal government or President Henrique Cardoso.
"It will definitely distract some attention from the discussions underway right now on reelection and administrative reforms," said Joyce Chang, emerging markets debt strategist at Merrill Lynch.
"We're watching very closely, but it doesn't seem like the mood there is panicked at this point," Chang added.
Jaime Valdivia, senior Latin America analyst at Morgan Stanley & Co, said his outlook on Brazil remains somewhat positive.
"We think this issue of the corruption scandal will not implicate President Cardoso," Valdivia said.
Elsewhere, Panama debt performed particularly well, with PDIs up 7/8 at 85-7/8 bid.
Continued speculation the country will issue a Eurobond and buy back a portion of its Brady debt helped spark the rally, analysts said.

"They have been talking, at least in the local papers, about issuing another Eurobond and using the procedes to buy back Brady bonds, which is what they did with their first Eurobond," Merrill's Chang said.

Bulgaria also surged, as an International Monetary Fund (IMF) delegation arrived in Sofia to help establish a fixed exchange rate and improve macroeconomic policies. Buoyed by late buying, Bulgaria FLRBs were up a full point at 51-1/8 bid.

"I think we're looking at one day in a string of days that will bring the Bulgarian strips close to or inside, say, Ecuador," said Eric Nielsen, a vice president and senior economist at Goldman Sachs. He said the market had known about the IMF mission for weeks, and prices notched higher on expected economic improvements.
More broadly, Argentina FRBs were off 1/8 at 92-3/8 bid, Mexico pars were off 1/8 at 74 bid and dollar-denominated Russian Vnesh loans were up 1/8 at 84 bid.
